result:
Round 281 passes. A's change does what the task asked, and I re-ran every check myself instead of relying on A's report. Nothing was committed or pushed, and I changed no app source.

**What the round does:** this round changed only the performance test harness, not the app. A failed demo sound now stops a test pass at once with a named error. Before, it ended in a generic 90 s or 15 s timeout. The click test also records which lanes it used, and the error text can no longer say "lane null". A's five code files are byte-identical to B's measured sketch. The doc edits stay inside the sections B allowed, and the frozen-file list matched at the start and at the end.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Typecheck | passes |
| Full perf run, alone | 3 passed in 13.9 min (PERF-1a 7.1 min, PERF-1b-i 5.4 min, PERF-1b-ii 1.1 min) |
| Equivalence with earlier results | 0 problems in all three specs; one value inside its allowed tolerance (65 → 65.1) |
| Lane ids in the click results | 6 of 6 samples: clip on `music`, empty click on `stems` |
| Lane ids in the real browser | after Add, `music` holds 1 clip and `stems` holds none, at 1440×900 and 1280×720 |
| Selected sound fails | every pass stops at load with the exact named error; whole run 9.3 s (before this change: 90 s per pass) |
| Another sound fails | every pass stops at load; the library-ready wait caught it in all 6 |
| Library-ready check disabled | every pass stops with the exact status-wait error, so that second check works too |
| Lane guard removed | the type check fails (TS2322 on the `clipTrackId` line), as expected |
| Sign-in is not bypassed | `/studio-lab` opens the demo with no sign-in; `/studio/middle-east` asks for sign-in and loads no audio; the Studio token endpoint returns 401 with no header and 500 with a fake token, never a token. Both viewports |

I also ran the real Studio flow in the browser: add a sound, play, stop, export. Audio was audible while playing, and the playhead advanced and then held. The exported WAV (48 kHz, 24-bit, stereo, 16.000 s) matches the reference hash from rounds 279–280, with no bad samples or dropouts.

**One Low finding for B (C-R281-01):** line 264 of the task cites lines 18, 34 and 71 of doc 208 without a claim tag, which the claims rule (L29) requires. I checked all three lines and they are true, so the round still passes. B should decide at the next retro whether such references need a tag.

**Environment note:** my untimed warm-up of `/studio-lab` after the heavy perf builds took longer than 180 s. This is the known cold-start pattern. The timed browser checks ran after it and loaded in 11 s and 6 s, so none of them is invalid.

**Still open, carried forward:** two Low review notes from A (how the combined status pattern is grouped; a second read of the status text), the PERF-1b-ii signal (B-R281-RESOURCES-READY-FAILED), and ROOT-REQ-PERF-TIMEOUT (PERF-1a uses about 47 % of its 15 min limit). The full test suite, build and verify belong to the root gate, and I did not claim them.

Files are in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- c-round-281.md
- c-round-281.json
- c-round-281/
